items.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Comparing it to Coltrane or something? ... [INTERVIEWEE] The avant garde, free jazz, funk, rock & roll.

ctx.x: He certainly doesn’t and he still lives in a hotel. But this Jazz Spotlight News was, I think, a very worthwhile venture in which everybody who contributed talked about the music and the field and the business, the affairs of music, just the way they felt. You know they weren’t politically motivated to lean toward one side or the other, they’d — straight ahead, exactly how they felt, pulling no punches. And when I wrote this article, “I’ll never make it big because my stuff is just too old fashioned,” was based…
Comparing it to Coltrane or something? Or the avant garde or free jazz?
The avant garde, free jazz, funk, rock & roll.

items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Talk about Coltrane for a minute. Did you know him personally? Did you have interactions? [INTERVIEWEE] Yes, I knew him personally.

ctx.x: I brag about having the same birthday as Trane. Where were we?
Well we can stop there, because first of all, happy birthday.
